system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review of Seller documents against Wattlebridge’s playbook**

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m). | 25% of price (AUD 6m). | **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6m.** The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval, which has not been given. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 aggregate basket, with only the excess recoverable. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject; counter to the playbook thresholds and tipping basket.** Seller’s thresholds materially narrow recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; proposes applying any limitation to all Claims unless stated otherwise. | 24 months after Completion for general claims, without extending that limit to categories with separate regimes. | **Reject; counter at 24 months and preserve separate claim regimes.** The 18-month fallback lacks required written approval. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; specify a separate regime.** Applying general limits would leave core ownership and authority claims under-protected. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Reject; add the full carve-out.** The playbook prohibits waiving these protections. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records, alongside specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure; no deemed disclosure merely from the whole data room, public registers or a prudent search. | **Reject; remove blanket deemed disclosure.** General disclosure could defeat warranties without identifying the relevant matters fairly. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from data room or public records. | Delete blanket knowledge exclusions; if any qualifier remains, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and never apply it to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject; delete the exclusion or narrow it strictly as above.** Data-room access or discoverability should not itself bar Buyer claims. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure says no final consent or evidence conditions are satisfied is included. | Effective consent **and evidence that its conditions are satisfied** before Completion; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient. | **Reject; make both consent and condition satisfaction a Completion requirement.** Delivery of consent alone does not establish that its conditions have been met. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure confirms it has not been repaid and no final security discharge is included. | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Reject post-Completion release as drafted; require payout and releases at Completion.** The outstanding debt and security should not be left unresolved without the specified approval and protection. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 bonuses are Seller’s matter and absent from the funds flow; on-costs are unspecified. | AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded. | **Require itemisation or Seller funding, including applicable on-costs.** The funds flow must not silently omit a disclosed Completion liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity is limited to SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. Disclosure says SOW3 materials transfer only after every fee is paid; AUD 180,000 open is not independently bank-verified, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is included. | Broaden the indemnity to address the transfer/ownership risk while preserving the SOW3 cure; do not treat AUD 180,000 as independently verified either way. | **Reject the narrow indemnity; broaden it and preserve the cure.** The disclosed payment and assignment evidence does not establish that the materials transferred. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Seller describes DD-006 as preliminary and not expected to be material. | Preserve logs, investigate and provide updates; do not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified demand. | **Require preservation, investigation and updates without asserting an unconfirmed outcome.** The disclosed record leaves access, scope and notification obligations unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate renewals are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess the three related renewals together for timing and scope; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Investigate and assess, but do not automatically classify as Debt or deduct from price.** The disclosure does not establish whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | Seller says Tax and IP are settled under the general regime; its limitation language applies to all Claims. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override. Tax/IP terms remain open, with no assumption of unlimited liability or resolution. | **Reject the blanket general-regime treatment; reserve Tax/IP and preserve category-specific terms.** The playbook keeps these categories separate and records no agreed resolution. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Seller relies on the Company share register at DD-012, which records it as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof. | **Require independent verification; do not accept DD-012 alone.** The register identifies the source relied on but does not independently verify the required title matters. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax/IP terms open for negotiation; assume neither unlimited liability nor a resolved position. | **Do not treat the terms as settled; reserve them for negotiation.** The Seller’s characterisation is not an agreed resolution under the playbook. |
=== END ADVICE ===
